A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same MF–IGB research, with matching central theorems, experiments and appendices A–H. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: V3 reports original signal-propagation simulations, classification training experiments and gradient analyses, including Figures 2 and 4 and Appendices B, E and G.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments and adds ResNet/MLP-Mixer correspondence tests and a pretrained-versus-untrained ViT gradient comparison.

M1.justification: The MF–IGB framework, initialization rules and training procedures are retained. The additional architecture tests and practical advice for locating the EOC do not establish a revised proposed algorithm or model.

E1.justification: Both versions use Gaussian synthetic inputs, binarized Fashion MNIST, binarized CIFAR10, CIFAR10 and CIFAR100, with ImageNet pretraining already present in v3. V4's added analyses use retained datasets and tasks; the changes concern model configurations and controls.

E2.justification: Appendix G.4.1 adds an untrained large ViT as a direct comparator to the pretrained ViT in Figure 29. V3's corresponding gradient analysis contains only pretrained variants. ResNet and MLP-Mixer are additional test architectures, rather than competing methods.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce an 18-layer ResNet, a reported 100-layer MLP-Mixer, and a matched untrained ViT control. Figure 29 compares gradients normalized at the final layer and also aggregated over four-layer blocks. The existing training settings in Table 2 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E.1 adds checks of MF–IGB agreement in production architectures, while Appendix G.4.1 tests how pretraining affects gradient stability. These extend the existing validation and sensitivity analyses. V4's main-text Figure 4 redisplays an existing appendix result and is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: The 90% MF intervals and dataset-median gradient summaries were already used in v3. V4 extends the interval convention to its new correspondence plots without introducing new seed counts, repeated-run information, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Figures 20–21 newly report MF–IGB agreement for ResNet and MLP-Mixer. Figure 29 shows stronger gradient explosion in the pretrained ViT than in its untrained counterpart. Figure 2 has updated empirical traces but retains its convergence findings; the existing training accuracy and bias trajectories are retained.

T1.justification: The central equivalence theorem, trainability proposition, and derivations in Appendices C–H retain their mathematical content and formal assumptions. Equation renumbering, notation cleanup and repaired cross-references do not constitute new theory. Appendix E.1 adds empirical validation, not a new proof.

C1.justification: The MF–IGB equivalence and biased-EOC claims remain central. V4 removes the explicit contribution connecting learnability with fairness, foregrounds class-dependent gradients as a contribution, and adds practical claims about bias absorption and hyperparameter-tuning duration.

C2.justification: V4 adds practical interpretations concerning short tuning runs and attributes greater gradient fragility to pretrained weights. It removes v3's concluding limitations paragraph about the ordered infinite-width/data limits and feature learning, while retaining the formal limiting assumptions in Section 2.1.

D1.justification: V4 adds a reproducibility statement linking code described as covering all simulations and training experiments. Appendix E.1 also supplies Timm model identification and access information. Existing optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size and pretrained-ViT details are retained; repository contents cannot be assessed from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The introduction replaces fairness and discrimination positioning with a substantially different discussion of MF theory, Tensor Programs, feature learning and practical training consequences. It adds Yang (2019, 2020), Yang and Hu (2021), and Francazi et al. (2023), while removing the fairness references and Zhang et al. (2021).

P1.justification: V4 substantially rewrites the abstract and introductory framing, changes the title, and reorganizes the opening around contributions and practical consequences. It adds concluding practical takeaways and a reproducibility statement while removing the limitations paragraph. The technical section sequence and most appendix prose remain stable.

P2.justification: V4 adopts ICLR formatting and running headers, redistributes floats and widens Figure 2. Figure 4 reproduces the ReLU portion of v3's Figure 22; Figures 20, 21 and 29 are new. Tables retain their structures, and most existing graphics are reused unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added production-architecture checks and pretrained/untrained control strengthen empirical support, while code-access information and practical explanations improve usability. Removing the explicit limitations paragraph makes scope constraints less prominent, although the formal assumptions remain stated. These changes provide a modest net improvement around the retained theoretical and experimental core.
